R0277.title: Robot Swarm Coordination Loss-of-Control Risk
R0277.definition: The risk that a multi-robot swarm, during collaborative tasks, loses coordinated control due to communication disruption, byzantine nodes, algorithm defects, or hijacked members, leading to swarm-behavior loss-of-control, task failure, or cascading physical harm.
R0277.description:
Robot swarm coordination loss-of-control risk can cause scaled destruction in warehouse, inspection, and military scenarios. The KARGU-2 lethal autonomous weapon system, per a 2021 UN report, had autonomous target tracking and swarm-coordination capabilities in the 2020 Libya civil war, operating fire-and-forget without an operator-munition data link — the first AI autonomous-weapon combat controversy. Individual hijacked swarm members become byzantine nodes that send false information to break consensus or have malicious coordination policies injected. Communication disruption desynchronizes the swarm; single-point failures are amplified by the swarm topology and are hard to stop via single-robot e-stop. In multi-agent reinforcement learning, Gleave et al. proved an adversary can defeat SOTA RL policies by its own behavior alone, without perturbing the victim's observations.

This risk relates to R0276 (robot physical harm & functional-safety failure), but is specialized for the swarm-coordination layer, emphasizing scaled loss-of-control and cascading harm.
R0277.influence: Swarm loss-of-control can cause scaled destruction in warehouse, inspection, and military scenarios; single-point failures are amplified by the swarm topology and are hard to stop via single-robot e-stop; autonomous-weapon swarms can make life-and-death decisions without meaningful human control.
